'''Adriana Lelia Calvo''' (16 December 1947 – 12 December 2010) was an Argentine physicist, university professor, and researcher. After being kidnapped by the military government during the [[National Reorganization Process|Argentine civil-military dictatorship]], she became a [[human rights]] activist, and was the first witness to testify at the [[Trial of the Juntas]] in 1985.

==Biography==
Adriana Calvo was born in Argentina in 1947. She earned a [[Licentiate (degree)#Argentina|licentiate]] in physics from the [[National University of La Plata]] (UNLP) in 1970. Until 1977, she worked as a teacher and researcher at UNLP's Faculty of Exact Sciences, after which she was a professor of physics at the Faculty of Engineering of the [[University of Buenos Aires]] (UBA). She was active in teachers' unions at both institutions, and is recognized as one of the main founders of the Asociación Gremial Docente (AGD).<ref name="La Capital">{{Cite news |url=https://www.lacapital.com.ar/politica/fallecioacute-adriana-calvo-dirigente-la-asociacioacuten-ex-detenidos-desaparecidos-n349717.html |title=Falleció Adriana Calvo, dirigente de la Asociación de Ex Detenidos Desaparecidos |trans-title=Adriana Calvo, Director of the Association of Former Disappeared Detainees, Passes Away |newspaper=[[La Capital]] |location=Buenos Aires |language=Spanish |date=2010-12-12 |access-date=2021-06-25}}</ref>

On 4 February 1977, she was arrested at her home in [[Tolosa, Buenos Aires|Tolosa]] by agents of the [[National Reorganization Process|civil-military dictatorship]].<ref name="Caso Nº 1">{{Cite web |url=http://www.derechos.org/nizkor/arg/causa13/casos/caso001.html |title=Caso Nº 1: Calvo de Laborde, Adriana |publisher=[[Equipo Nizkor]] |language=Spanish |access-date=2021-06-25}}</ref> At the time, she was six months pregnant.<ref name="La Capital"/><ref name=Tracing>{{Cite news |url=https://lens.blogs.nytimes.com/2010/05/28/showcase-167/ |title=Tracing the Shadows of Operation Condor |first=Daniel J. |last=Wakin |website=[[The New York Times]] Lens blog |date=2010-05-28 |access-date=2021-06-24}}</ref> Her husband, the chemist {{ill|Miguel Ángel Laborde|es}} (a professor at the UBA Faculty of Engineering and a [[National Scientific and Technical Research Council|CONICET]] researcher), was also detained.

Calvo was held clandestinely in various offices of the [[Buenos Aires Provincial Police]]: the Investigation Brigade of the City of [[La Plata]], the Arana Police Detachment, the 5th Police Station of La Plata, and the Banfield Investigation Brigade, called "[[Pozo de Banfield]]".<ref name="Caso Nº 1"/> During her transfer to the latter, she gave birth to her third daughter while handcuffed in the back of a military car.<ref name="La Capital"/><ref name=Tracing/>

Calvo and her newborn daughter were released on 28 April 1977.<ref name="Caso Nº 1"/> Immediately afterward, she tried to communicate with the families of other detainees. In the case of Inés Ortega and her son born in captivity, she asked her UNLP colleague, physicist [[Ana Buenaventura Mocoroa]], for help.<ref name="La Capital"/> She was the first witness at the [[Trial of the Juntas]] in 1985.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1989/10/09/world/pardon-of-argentine-officers-angers-critics-of-the-military.html |title=Pardon of Argentine Officers Angers Critics of the Military |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |agency=Reuters |page=A3 |date=1989-10-09 |access-date=2021-06-24}}</ref> She continued to advocate for human rights, becoming a leader of the {{ill|Association of Former Disappeared Detainees|es|Asociación de Ex Detenidos Desaparecidos}} (AEDD).<ref name=reclamo>{{Cite news |url=https://www.pagina12.com.ar/diario/sociedad/3-159654-2010-12-31.html |title=Un reclamo que se abre a otros reclamos |trans-title=A Claim That Opens Up Other Claims |first=Pedro |last=Lipcovich |newspaper=[[Página/12]] |language=Spanish |date=2010-12-31 |access-date=2021-06-24}}</ref>

After her release, Calvo continued her academic life. She obtained her PhD in physics at UNLP in 1993. She was in turn director of two doctoral students at the UBA Faculty of Engineering between 1996 and 2002. Their theses dealt with [[Porous medium|porous media]] and [[granular materials]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://www.fi.uba.ar/archivos/inv_doct_tesis_finalizadas.doc |title=Doctorado de la Universidad de Buenos Aires en Ingeniería |trans-title=Doctorate of the University of Buenos Aires in Engineering |publisher=[[University of Buenos Aires]] |pages=1–2 |language=Spanish |access-date=2021-06-25 |archive-date=24 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624203842/http://www.fi.uba.ar/archivos/inv_doct_tesis_finalizadas.doc |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Adriana Calvo died in [[Buenos Aires]] on 12 December 2010.<ref name=reclamo/>

==Legacy==
Her death was mourned by human rights organizations, her colleagues, and the community in general. Among the numerous notices was a profile published by the three children that Adriana had with Miguel Ángel Laborde,<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.pagina12.com.ar/diario/elpais/1-183246-2011-12-13.html |title=El recuerdo de Adriana Calvo |trans-title=The Memory of Adriana Calvo |first1=Santiago |last1=Laborde |first2=Martina |last2=Laborde |first3=Teresa |last3=Laborde |newspaper=[[Página/12]] |language=Spanish |date=2011-12-13 |access-date=2021-06-25}}</ref> and a recognition by the Senator [[Norma Morandini]], who wrote:

{{Blockquote|We will never finish thanking and acknowledging those survivors who, overcoming their own fear, reduced to numbers and silence, regained their legal status and recounted their ordeal before the five judges. Those of us who were there will never forget the testimony of Adriana Calvo, who, handcuffed and bandaged, had her baby on the side of a road. Adriana turned her ordeal into a fighting force and was one of the voices in solidarity with the tragedies of others.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.normamorandini.com.ar/?p=1135 |title=Homenaje a Adriana Calvo de Laborde |trans-title=Tribute to Adriana Calvo de Laborde |publisher=[[Norma Morandini]] |language=Spanish |date=2010-12-15 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331234741/http://www.normamorandini.com.ar/?p=1135 |archive-date=2019-03-31 |url-status=dead |access-date=2021-06-25}}</ref>}}

On 17 May 2011, Calvo was honored with a series of activities in her memory at [[ESPCI Paris]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://afaba.df.uba.ar/?p=633 |title=Homenaje en París a Adriana Calvo |trans-title=Tribute to Adriana Calvo in Paris |publisher=Asociación Física Argentina, Filial Buenos Aires |language=Spanish |date=2011-05-16 |access-date=2021-06-25}}</ref>
